key_insight: The paper shows that replacing per-sample data weights with a transferable selection network is promising, but only if trained with a new pointwise value-matching loss rather than standard meta-learning objectives.
engineering_relevance: TESS offers a scalable way to score and select training data for large language models across datasets and model sizes, making data curation more practical for safety and instruction tuning.
method: Introduces Transferable Example Scoring and Selection (TESS) for learned data selection.
Uses Pointwise Value Matching (PVM) instead of direct incorporation into existing MTS losses.
Targets stability and transferability by avoiding weight suppression and over-reliance on easy features.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong transfer across datasets, from subsets to full corpora, and from smaller to larger models on LLM safety and targeted instruction tuning.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is that directly plugging a selection network into existing meta-learning objectives can cause unstable optimization and poor generalization.
paper_title: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)
